summary.text: Crowborough Beacon is an undulating heathland course in East Sussex with panoramic views of the South Downs.

setting.text: The course lies on the southern slopes of the East Sussex High Weald, 800ft above sea level.
Top100golfcourses compares it to its neighbour Royal Ashdown Forest, with spectacular views across the treetops and springy, firm heathland turf, but notes there are bunkers here.
It measures a little over 6,200 yards, and Top100golfcourses says accuracy matters more than length, with small greens.

history.text: Golf began in 1895 with nine holes on the Alchorne estate, and the course was extended to 18 holes in 1905.
Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, creator of Sherlock Holmes, lived nearby and was club captain in 1910.
The original designer is unknown. A 1926 Bernard Darwin book on the club says Alister MacKenzie redesigned eight holes, so the club is listed among MacKenzie courses.

trivia.text: The signature hole is a par 3 called 'The Speaker', 190 yards from the back tees, played across a gully with a large pit left of the green.

local.text: The club is in Crowborough, East Sussex (postcode TN6), near Royal Ashdown Forest.
